metrics.description: Fraction of the 4 opcode operations (add, sub, and, or) correctly identified and implemented, measured via per-opcode simulation pass/fail.
metrics.name: word_recovery_rate

metrics.description: Degree to which the recovered module's port list and combinational structure conform to the pinned interface (module name, port widths, purely combinational).
metrics.name: structural_match_accuracy

metrics.description: Percentage of randomized+directed (a,b,sel) test vectors for which recovered_datapath output matches the reference gate_netlist.v output exactly, via iverilog/vvp simulation.
metrics.name: functional_equivalence

acceptance_criteria: All FR1-FR4 checks pass for a randomized + directed test vector sweep spanning at least 200 (a,b,sel) combinations including edge cases (0, 255, overflow/underflow points).
The baseline (empty/naive) submission fails at least one functional check, demonstrating the benchmark discriminates correct recoveries from trivial stubs.
No static-only pass path exists: correctness is determined solely by simulated output comparison against the reference gate netlist.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: gate_netlist.v is a flattened bit-blasted implementation of: y = sel==00 ? a+b : sel==01 ? a-b : sel==10 ? (a&b) : (a|b), built from a ripple-carry adder/subtractor (via XOR-conditional invert + carry chain) and gate-level AND/OR arrays, with a 4-way bit-sliced multiplexer selecting among the four bit-computed results per output bit. The bit-blasting deliberately interleaves adder carry logic with the mux select wires so that no single gate cluster visibly corresponds to 'add' or 'subtract' â the reverse engineer must trace carry propagation across all 8 bit-slices to recognize the arithmetic structure.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Directed testbench vectors with known non-commutative (a,b) pairs (e.g., a=5,b=3 and a=3,b=5) distinguish add-vs-sub and correct operand order; failures here indicate CWE-697 (Incorrect Comparison) style logic-recovery mistakes leading to wrong opcode mapping.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered module must not silently default to an incorrect operation for select codes 00 or 01 (e.g., mixing up add and subtract, or computing b-a instead of a-b), since this reflects a common reverse-engineering error of misreading the carry-in/invert convention.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Test boundary cases (a=255,b=1 for add overflow; a=0,b=1 for subtract underflow) and verify y wraps modulo 256 with no extraneous bits set, guarding against CWE-682 (Incorrect Calculation) style width-recovery errors.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered netlist's arithmetic width and wraparound behavior (8-bit modulo arithmetic, no extra carry-out bit leaking into y) must match the original, since an incorrect width recovery could expose or misrepresent internal carry state.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An adversary (or IP thief) is given only the flattened gate netlist without word-level annotations. They must reconstruct the high-level word-level semantics (the opcode-to-operation mapping) purely from gate topology and simulation, which is exactly the reverse-engineering task; a naive or incomplete recovery (e.g., only recovering AND/OR but guessing add/sub wrong sign convention, or swapping add/sub select codes) should fail functional equivalence checks.

constraints: The submission must not modify any file under inputs/.
The recovered_datapath module must be purely combinational (no clocked always blocks, no latches).
The design must not instantiate or depend on any vendor-specific primitives; only standard Verilog constructs are allowed.
The output y must be driven for every combination of sel; undefined sel values (there are none beyond 2'b00-2'b11) need not be handled specially.
expected_outputs: A single Verilog file submission/recovered_rtl.v containing a module named recovered_datapath with the exact port list specified in the interface.
The recovered module must reproduce the output of gate_netlist.v for all 4 select values across a broad sweep of operand values.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted module recovered_datapath must compile cleanly with iverilog alongside a generated testbench with no syntax or elaboration errors.
For select=2'b00, the module output y must equal a+b (8-bit wraparound, no carry-out port) for all tested (a,b) pairs.
For select=2'b01, the module output y must equal a-b (8-bit wraparound, two's complement) for all tested (a,b) pairs.
For select=2'b10 the output y must equal (a & b), and for select=2'b11 the output y must equal (a | b), for all tested (a,b) pairs.

public_spec.interface: File: submission/recovered_rtl.v must define exactly one module named 'recovered_datapath' with port list: module recovered_datapath(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, input [1:0] sel, output [7:0] y); Ports: a (8-bit, public operand A), b (8-bit, public operand B), sel (2-bit, public opcode select: 00=add,01=sub,10=and,11=or per functional requirements), y (8-bit, public result output). No additional ports, no clock, purely combinational. The module must be synthesizable/simulatable standalone (no external includes beyond standard Verilog).
public_spec.objective: You are given a flattened, bit-level gate netlist of a small combinational datapath with two 8-bit data inputs, a 2-bit select input, and an 8-bit output. The netlist was produced by bit-blasting a word-level design into primitive gates (AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR, NOT, and multiplexers built from these), which obscures the original word-level operation performed for each select value. Your job is to analyze the netlist and produce a clean, word-level Verilog module that is functionally equivalent to the original gate-level design for every possible input combination.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.

title: Recover a MUX-based ALU Datapath's Word-Level Function
